name: Denoising using LPCA
summary: Denoises a DWI series with the DIPY 1.1.1 local PCA (dipy_denoise_lpca) workflow and outputs the denoised DWI with its bvals and bvecs.
description: Wraps the DIPY 1.1.1 command-line workflow dipy_denoise_lpca, which removes noise by thresholding local principal components using the gradient table. Use it as an optional early DWI preprocessing step before model fitting. It needs a DWI with bvals/bvecs; the gradient files are copied unchanged to the output.

inputs.description: Diffusion-weighted image (NIfTI) with its bvals and bvecs files.

outputs.description: Denoised DWI (dwi.nii.gz) with the original bvals and bvecs.

parameters.description: Standard deviation of the noise estimated from the data. A value of 0 means sigma value estimation with the Manjon2013 algorithm
The radius of the local patch to be taken around each voxel (in voxels). Default: 2 (denoise in blocks of 5x5x5 voxels).

Use either eigenvalue decomposition ('eig') or singular value decomposition ('svd') for principal component analysis. The default method is 'eig' which is faster. However, occasionally 'svd' might be more accurate.

citations.text: Garyfallidis E, et al. Dipy, a library for the analysis of diffusion MRI data. Front Neuroinform 8:8 (2014).
Avesani P, et al. The open diffusion data derivatives, brain data upcycling via integrated publishing of derivatives and reproducible open cloud services. Sci Data 6:69 (2019).
